# Project context (optional)
# Add only constraints that should guide OpenSpec artifacts and workflows.
# Include constraints an agent cannot infer by reading the code.
# Keep general project documentation and discoverable codebase facts out.
# Example:
#   context: |
#     Designs and tasks must cover Windows, macOS, and Linux
#     Write all artifacts in Spanish

# Per-artifact rules (optional)
# Add custom rules for specific artifacts.
# Example:
#   rules:
#     proposal:
#       - Keep proposals under 500 words
#       - Always state what is out of scope
#     tasks:
#       - Break tasks into chunks of max 2 hours

# Per-operation guidance (optional)
# Add advisory guidance for how apply and archive work should be conducted.

# Example:
#   operations:
#     apply:
#       guidance:
#         - Keep test summaries concise
#     archive:
#       guidance:
#         - Summarize the archive outcome before finishing

# 5. docs/customization.md of OpenSpec v1.16.0 (quotes):
source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/v1.16.0/docs/customization.md (tag v1.16.0), fetched with curl on 2026-11-10
sha256: adfc1277bab095289812bd3224010f362855c633796a7a928a155623916a8386
lines: 435

--- lines 13 to 47 (Project Configuration, Quick Setup)
13: ## Project Configuration
14: 
15: The `openspec/config.yaml` file is the easiest way to customize OpenSpec for your team. It lets you:
16: 
17: - **Set a default schema** - Skip `--schema` on every command
18: - **Inject project context** - AI sees your tech stack, conventions, etc.
19: - **Add per-artifact rules** - Custom rules for specific artifacts
20: - **Add per-operation guidance** - Advisory preferences for apply and archive work
21: - **Remember integration choices** - e.g. the [GitHub Copilot cloud coding agent](supported-tools.md#github-copilot-cloud-coding-agent) opt-in
22: 
23: ### Quick Setup
24: 
25: ```bash
26: openspec init
27: ```
28: 
29: This walks you through creating a config interactively. Or create one manually:
30: 
31: ```yaml
32: # openspec/config.yaml
33: schema: spec-driven
34: 
35: context: |
36:   Tech stack: TypeScript, React, Node.js, PostgreSQL
37:   API style: RESTful, documented in docs/api.md
38:   Testing: Jest + React Testing Library
39:   We value backwards compatibility for all public APIs
40: 
41: rules:
42:   proposal:
43:     - Include rollback plan
44:     - Identify affected teams
45:   specs:
46:     - Use Given/When/Then format
47:     - Reference existing patterns before inventing new ones

--- lines 75 to 96 (Context and rules injection)
75: **Context and rules injection:**
76: 
77: When generating any artifact, your context and rules are injected into the AI prompt:
78: 
79: ```xml
80: <context>
81: Tech stack: TypeScript, React, Node.js, PostgreSQL
82: ...
83: </context>
84: 
85: <rules>
86: - Include rollback plan
87: - Identify affected teams
88: </rules>
89: 
90: <template>
91: [Schema's built-in template]
92: </template>
93: ```
94: 
95: - **Context** appears in ALL artifacts
96: - **Rules** ONLY appear for the matching artifact
